utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody. Please be seated. May I ask the usher to escort the witness into the courtroom immediately. Thank you. During the time, may we hear the case number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. This is case number IT-97-24-T, the Prosecutor versus Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Nicholas Koumjian, Ann Sutherland, and Ruth Karper for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And for the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Branko Lukic and Danilo Cirkovic for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And then the witness of today appeared as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Mr. Vila, good morning to you as well. You know you gave us yesterday your solemn declaration. No doubt this is valid also today. So Mr. Koumjian, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: If I could ask the usher just to move the ELMO back a little bit so we're not... Cross-examined by Mr. Koumjian: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me, sir, were you ever the most powerful politician in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within the political party that I belonged to - that was the SDP - for a while I was the executive secretary, and I was professionally employed in that party and I received a salary there. Later on I was the vice-president of the municipal board of the Socialist Party of Republika Srpska and the main board of the Socialist Party of Republika Srpska, but that was later on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hold what you considered to be the most powerful political position - I'm not talking about party position - but position in the civilian politics in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time in the executive government the most powerful position was the president of the executive board, and today it is the mayor, according to the new law on local administration.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So your position is that in 1997 and 1998, when you were president of the executive board, you were the most powerful political figure in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say that I was a political figure. It was a figure belonging to the executive part of the functioning of the administration and the relationship with the population and with the economic subjects. It belongs to the area of the application of laws and the exercise of the rights of citizens.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time, which political party did you belong to, in 1997-1998?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time I belonged to the Socialist Party of Republika Srpska. That is correct. And as its candidate, after the verification of the election result, I was appointed to the aforementioned position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Socialist Party of Republika Srpska hold the most seats in the Prijedor Municipal Assembly of any party at the time of your appointment to the executive board?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that period, the Socialist Party of Republika Srpska was the second ranking party in Prijedor municipality, after the SDS. And we were followed by the Party for Krajina and Posavina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So in 1997, when you became the president of the executive board, can you remind me -- I was a little bit unclear -- when did you become the president of the executive board? At what -- during what month in 1997?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that the implementation and my appointment to that position was in November of 1997.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to being appointed the president of the executive board, were you a member of the assembly or did you hold another position earlier in 1997?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was on the list of my party as a deputy, and as a deputy I was given a seat in the assembly. However, one cannot be a deputy and a member of the executive branch of the government. These two are incompatible, and that is why I had to return my seat of a deputy, and I was replaced by the second ranking after me in the municipal assembly, and I went to the executive branch of the government.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. So my understanding is that in 1997, in November, when you took the position of president of the executive board, the SDS party was the leading party in the Prijedor Municipal Assembly in -- within the Republika Srpska Prijedor --

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who held the position at that time of president of the municipal assembly?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time the president of the municipal assembly was Mr. Borislav Maric, a member of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you've testified here in court that the president of the executive board was a more powerful position than the president of the municipal assembly. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've also told us -- we know that in 1990, after the 1990 elections, the SDA won the most seats in the assembly and was awarded the position of president of the municipal assembly, and the second party received the position of president of the executive board, that being the SDS. We know from your testimony this morning that in 1997 the leading party was the SDS and they received the position of president of the municipal assembly, and the second party, your party, received the position of president of the executive board. Can you explain, sir --

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why is -- thank you. Can you explain, sir, why it is that the leading party would not take the leading position in the municipality in both 1992 and 1997?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you about 1992 because I was not a member of the interparty agreement on the implementation and the distribution of power. But about 1997 I can tell you that at the time the interparty agreement took quite a long time and that agreement ended up with the distribution of various areas. According to the law, they could ask for certain sectors, and the minority population had the right to 20 per cent of the seats in the executive government. In the interparty agreement, the first thing that the SDS asked for was the president of the executive board, the secretary-general of the municipal assembly, and the chief of the sector for economy. These are the most powerful positions, and this could not reflect the total SDS result in the elections. They insisted on being awarded the position of the secretary-general of the municipal assembly and the chief of the sector for economy. Finally, the SDS accepted for their candidate to be appointed the secretary-general of the municipal assembly, the president of the municipal assembly, and the secretary of the sector for economy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, in 1997 in the assembly in Prijedor, in the beginning of that year, who was the president of the assembly?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean before the elections?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's talk about the -- from January through July of 1997. Who was the president of the municipal assembly of Prijedor -- 1997?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it was Dusan Kurnoga.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, sir, let me try to remind you. Wasn't it Milomir Stakic who was the president of the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor in 1997?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't remember the dates when people were removed and replaced and when new people came into positions. It's very difficult for me to remember those dates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you do remember that after the war in 1996 and 1997, Dr. Stakic was again the president of the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor. Correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you have reminded me, and yes, I can say that this is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And it's correct, is it not, that Dr. Stakic represented -- he was the candidate of the SDS party at that time; correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I believe so. I believe that he was an SDS candidate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the SDS at that time controlled the -- had the most seats in the Prijedor Municipal Assembly. They had the majority of seats; correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to cause Dr. Stakic to no longer be the president of the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor in 1997?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Mr. Borislav Maric who was the candidate for the president of the municipal assembly. He was elected on the proposal of the SDS. And upon the expiry of his mandate, I believe that Dr. Stakic returned to the position of the CEO in the health centre or a doctor in the health centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So if I understand your answer, you believe that Dr. Stakic at the end of his mandate -- you believe it expired sometime in 1997 and then he returned to work in the Prijedor health centre?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that this is what happened. There were the elections, that -- one set of mandates expired, and that the new set of mandates was put in place and was implemented.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me suggest some things to you and you tell me whether these remind you of events that took place back in 1997, some five or six years ago. Do you recall that in July of 1997 Dr. Stakic was the president of the municipal assembly and in the middle of that month SFOR arrested Mico Kovacevic -- Dr. Milan Kovacevic and attempted to arrest and during that attempted arrest killed Simo Drljaca? Do you recall those events taking place in Prijedor in July 1997?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember the arrest of Dr. Kovacevic and him being taken away. I also remember the incident in which Simo Drljaca was killed, but I'm not aware of the fact that it was -- that there was a failed attempt to arrest Dr. Stakic. I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I hope -- I don't believe I stated that, so let me -- I believe I said an attempt to arrest Mr. Drljaca. Sir, did you ever see Dr. Stakic after that day when Mr. Kovacevic was arrested?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: On one or two occasions I saw him in the health centre in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the months that that took place?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't recall that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Dr. Stakic -- let me try -- suggest something to you and tell you -- and you can tell me if it reminds you. Did Dr. Stakic leave the position of president of the municipal assembly before the expiration of his term?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so, because the implementation of the results was in November 1997 and from the June events to November, I don't remember that Dr. Stakic was physically in the position of the president of the municipal assembly and that he discharged the duties of the president of the municipal assembly. I believe that acting president of the municipal assembly was Mr. Radanovic, who at the time held the position of the vice-president of the municipal assembly and who, when the president was absent, would take the place of the president. Now, as for the real reasons for the president's absence during that time, I wouldn't be able to tell you what those were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, Mr. Radanovic, who you just mentioned, is that Momcilo Radanovic, nicknamed Cigo?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Mr. Radanovic one of those persons you referred to -- well, excuse me. Can I -- perhaps we can go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I can see no objections. Private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: One second. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, did you know Dr. Stakic outside of the municipal assembly? Did you know him socially or professionally in other ways?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was an acquaintance, and I didn't know him before I met him in the assembly. He was not my physician. We never socialised outside the building of the municipal assembly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you run into him around the town? Would you see him in public places?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very rarely. I saw him maybe once or twice when he was playing snooker in a restaurant. He was in the company of two or three young men or men of his age whom I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your observations of -- excuse me. Did you ever go to his office in 1992? Did you ever go to the office of the president of the municipal assembly?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. It may have been once or twice. When I represented my group of deputies, when we were talking about the agenda of the upcoming session. But this was not me talking to him, but I was always accompanied by other people and there was always the secretary-general of the municipal assembly present there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you describe Dr. Stakic and your knowledge of him professionally as being an intelligent person?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is very hard to judge somebody who is of a different profession, who comes from a different walk of life. I believe that he was a promising doctor, and I believe that as a young and inexperienced person he was pushed into the politics and he wasn't aware of how politics worked. He was politically inexperienced when he was pushed into that sphere of life.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you haven't answered my question. Do you believe Dr. Stakic was an intelligent person? Can you answer that.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of an average intelligence, I would say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your dealings with Dr. Stakic, would he listen to other individuals?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have said, and I will repeat that. Whenever I met Dr. Stakic, it was in connection with the preparations for the upcoming session of the assembly. We were talking about the items on the agenda. And as far as I could notice, he would listen to the proposers, be it the executive board or some other proposers. He would listen to their suggestions. He would accept their suggestions. And together with the secretary-general of the assembly, he would finalise the preparations for the session. The secretary-general was in charge of preparing all the technical details of the upcoming session of the assembly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your contacts with Dr. Stakic when he presided over the municipal assembly in 1992 and later, when -- after the war ended, of the Dayton Agreements, you indicated you attended about 80 per cent of the assembly sessions or more -- did he appear to be a president who was informed about events that were taking place in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on what was presented to the local parliament, it is my impression that he was aware of what was taking place in Prijedor. During the assembly session, he would also give introductory remarks and explanations on various items of the agenda. As the president of the municipal assembly, he was very correct in his presiding over the session. He would give the floor to everybody who asked the floor and he would give everybody the opportunity to express their views.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As the president of the executive board in 1997, your office was on the same floor as the office of the president, is that correct, the same floor of the municipal assembly building?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the president of the municipal assembly and the president of the executive board receive media - for example, Kozarski Vjesnik, Glas newspapers - and official documents like the Official Gazettes of Prijedor in order to keep informed of the events?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time I believe that Kozarski Vjesnik, Glas, and Oslobodenje were the papers that were ordered and received. And as for the Official Gazette, the Official Gazette was received by the technical services who had to be abreast of the new laws and their implementation. So the Official Gazette was mostly received and followed by the secretary-general and his staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you as the president of the executive board could request reports. And in fact, you yourself testified you requested reports from the security services regarding their activities, and they responded and reported to you. Correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very rarely at that time. Maybe once or twice throughout the whole mandate we discussed the security issues at a session of the assembly. For a simple relation, political relationships were stabilised, the implementation was in place. We had some more urgent things to discuss. And at that time the political and security situation was already stable. Refugees started coming back. The situation between the people and various ethnic groups, started improving. And that's why we didn't discuss the security situation that much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 46 of yesterday's LiveNote, line 5, you said: "I did request some reports on the political and security situation and the security of the citizens. I never requested anything else, any other reports, and there are no other contacts." And the question that you were responding to had to do with giving orders to the Ministry of the Interior. So sir, did you request from the police or Ministry of the Interior reports, and did they respond and give you those reports?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that there has been a misunderstanding. While I was in the position of the president of the executive board and earlier on, the executive board could not order anything to the Ministry of the Interior or ask from them to do certain things. The only thing that we could ask from them was a report on the political and security situation for the assembly session. As far as I can remember, throughout all of my mandate it -- such a report was considered at an assembly session once or maybe twice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me repeat the question. Did you ask for reports from the Ministry of the Interior and did you receive those reports that you asked for?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Repeat. Once or twice throughout my entire mandate a request was filed with the Ministry of the Interior to report on the political and security situation, and they sent us the report and it was discussed, but I can't remember at what session of the assembly was it that we discussed such a report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, yesterday you discussed on your direct examination the duties of the president of the municipal assembly, and you listed certain limited duties, setting the agenda, presiding over the sessions, representing the municipality when there were delegations of dignitaries or special events. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the president of the assembly also speak to the media? Did he represent the assembly in the media?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, some of his duties concerning managing the work of the assembly, yes. Concerning those subjects he did speak to the media.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you talk about delegations, would that be, for example, a delegation from Banja Luka of regional leaders coming to Prijedor, that they would be met by the president of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Usually the president of the assembly did host such delegations during my term of office as the executive board. But the president of the executive board and the secretary-general of the municipality were always there too. Usually there was a group of three or four representatives of the local community hosting such delegations. That -- welcoming such delegations. That also depended on the type of delegation that was arriving. Were they from the republican organs? Was that an international delegation? Usually a protocol would be drawn up and an agenda would be set with subjects to be discussed so that adequate preparations could be made.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall in the summer of 1992 Radoslav Brdjanin, who was then the president of the Crisis Staff for the Autonomous Region of Krajina visited Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was not a guest of the parliament. Now, whether he was welcomed at the building of the municipal assembly, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you present during his visit at any time, to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've described these rather limited duties of the president of the municipal assembly. You told us that this is a professional position, so it's a position that he's given a salary for, as opposed to the nominal salary that normal deputies get; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Given how limited the duties are that you described, why is it that this is a full-time position? What does the president do all day?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in addition to problems related to the work of the assembly and its sessions, as well as the amount of coordination involved in setting up an assembly meeting, during his regular working hours the president of the assembly must prepare all these tasks. Part of his time goes to receiving parties and clients, citizens requesting to see the president of the assembly, requesting to see the president of the executive board too in order to exercise some of their rights which were not included in the regular procedure. Or, for example, if citizens wanted to lodge complaints concerning certain phenomenon or certain officials, the behaviour of certain officials.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So part of the duty of the president of the municipality -- the municipal assembly is to make sure that the concerns of citizens of Prijedor reach that assembly; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, were you ever a member of the National Defence Council in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. My position during the time when I was president of the executive board, there was no such body at that time according to the then-existing regulations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1992, did you attend any meetings after the takeover of the National Defence Council?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never attended any of these meetings. And I don't know who the members of the council are supposed to be. At any rate, as a deputy I never attended any such meetings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Fine. Then I won't ask you further questions about that. Sir, at the municipal assembly sessions that you attended, during the time period that Dr. Stakic was the president of the municipality, did you discuss providing what aid the municipality could to these refugees from places like Croatia, from Zagreb, from Knin, from other parts of Central Bosnia that were coming to Prijedor? Did you discuss providing aid to those persons?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think this was discussed at any of the sessions of the assembly. On one or two occasions certain reports were received from a special centre recording the incoming refugees. Probably it was through humanitarian organisations or in some other way that these problems were being dealt with. It was not part of the decision-making process of the local parliament. Information was received on several occasions about the growing numbers of incoming refugees and the lack of adequate facilities to put them up, but the situation at that time was a very high unemployment rate and a desperate economic situation in general.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, what crimes -- you mentioned yesterday a murder that you were aware of that occurred after the takeover of a reserve policeman. What other crimes are you aware of that occurred after the takeover from the 30th of April through the end of September 1992?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say for certain whether it was on the 30th of May or between the 29th and 30th of May. Certain paramilitary units from the direction of the old town tried to storm the local information media, the Kozarski Vjesnik and the local radio station, the municipality building, and the MUP building. There were casualties there. I think the attackers suffered casualties too, as well as those who were defending these institutions and buildings. I know where in town exactly these buildings are, but I don't really remember where I was on that particular day, so I was not an eyewitness to these events. I learned about these events from the media and by talking to friends and colleagues. Members of the families of those who had lost their lives in these incidents also told me about the whole thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you finished?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, in addition to this incident that you're talking about, the attempt by Muslims and Croats to reverse the takeover of the 30th of April and to violently get rid of the authorities in Prijedor, are there other crimes that you're aware of?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were quite many attempts. There was a war on, so there were a number of murders. There were a number of murders where persons of the same ethnic background killed each other or maybe there were paramilitary soldiers killing people. The times were unsafe. Given the nature of my job in one of the companies I worked for or as a deputy to the municipal assembly, I had no need for direct contact or to monitor these events. And aside from that, it has been quite a long time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, sir, I gather from your answer to my last two questions that aside from the murder of a reserve officer that you remember and the attack that you told us about, you're not aware of any crimes committed by the Army of Republika Srpska, by the police in Prijedor, and the civilian authorities in Prijedor against Muslim and Croat citizens of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were a number of military operations and activities in the area of the so-called Brdo following events in Hambarine and Kozarac. However, this is between 7 and 12 kilometres outside Prijedor. And aside from people who were there in the actual area witnessing these events, it was very difficult to know anything for sure if you were in Prijedor or somewhere even further away. I do know that part of the population was killed during those military operations. But under what circumstances exactly and how many, I really can't be -- I really can't tell you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you drove from Prijedor to Ljubija, you passed through the Brdo region; correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up to the events in Hambarine and following those events, it was quite risky to go there, to pass through that area. So for a month or two I didn't go to Ljubija. The only way I spoke to the guards from Miska Glava and Vojavi [phoen], was by telephone. I'm referring to the guards from my company, the security guards. They would walk to the company premises and we'd arrange things through Jakara Marina, a secretary who lived in Ljubija. And our only concern that time was to keep our premises from being invaded and our property from being looted. It was only after a month or two, a month or two after the operations and the clashes in the Brdo area - I'm talking about Hambarine, Rizvanovici, Biscani, and Rakovcani - that I took the road to Donja Ljubija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, I'm going to move on, and I'm now going to ask you questions not having to do with your own personal knowledge of events but with what you heard during municipal assembly meetings presided over by Dr. Stakic. At these meetings, did you discuss removing the non-Serb population from Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Discussions during assembly sessions or decisions of the assembly or conclusions of the assembly never, at least as far as the sessions I attended were concerned, included any such subjects. All the decisions and conclusions of the assembly were published in the Official Gazette of the municipality, so it's possible even now to verify if any such decisions had ever been made.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the decisions and conclusions are published, but the discussions, what people said, is not published in the gazette; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection, what was reviewed during one of the assembly sessions was a report by the Crisis Staff related to the period of time when the assembly was not meeting. So you have this report marked with the exact date and entry number, as well as its subject, so such decisions were then verified. But discussions focussing on such issues, no, there were no such discussions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, were there discussions about organising convoys from Trnopolje and other locations to take non-Serbs out of the Prijedor municipality?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with any such conclusions by the assembly, conclusions to that effect, but I know that a number of people were leaving Prijedor. I know because people talked about this. And there were collection centres for those who were found innocent of any crimes and had expressed their desire to leave Prijedor and go to a different place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you vote to confirm the decisions of the Crisis Staff at the meeting of the municipal assembly on the 24th of July, I believe, 1992?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The end of July, yes. I remember it was the end of July. I can't remember the exact date. Most deputies agreed and ratified the conclusions and decisions of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Perhaps the witness could be given Exhibit 250, S250.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While that's being handed out -- sir, if you could take a look at this document. It's number S250. Do you recognise this as the decision of the municipal assembly from late July 1992 wherein the decisions of the Crisis Staff were confirmed?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection, this precisely was the material used at the assembly and this is the way it was handed out to the deputies. There were no introductory remarks. There was no discussion even, I believe. I think the assembly, that is, the majority of the deputies, were informed about this section and the deputies then ratified the conclusions and decisions of the Crisis Staff in the interim period between the two assembly sessions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any discussion, debate, or disagreements regarding these decisions?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I already said, I don't think there was a discussion as such during that session concerning these issues. These were handed out to the deputies. They were asked whether they had any objections or questions. There were none, so this was ratified in its original form. I think the deputies understood this more as a form of report on the enactments adopted by the Crisis Staff in the meantime, which had already been implemented and which received ratification, official ratification in this way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall Dr. Stakic making any negative comments or any objections to these decisions?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember any objections or comments.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, did the municipal assembly appoint judges in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The judges of the basic court are appointed by the Ministry of Justice. I think the municipality only appoints the judge for the -- the misdemeanour judge. But I'm not sure exactly what sort of influence they have in that particular appointment. The judiciary is independent from the local, legislative, and executive authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. If the witness could be given S259, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, just take your time and familiarise yourself a bit with this document, and then I'd ask you to turn when you're ready, to point to number 8, Roman numeral VIII. Not the agenda 8 but the Roman numeral VIII. Would it be correct, sir, that you were appointed, according to this document, to the commission on elections -- excuse me, to the elections and appointments board? I'm sorry, it's --

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I gave you the wrong -- 13, Roman numeral XIII. Yes. So, sir, were you appointed to the elections and appointments board which was headed by Mr. Savanovic?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a regular commission of the assembly, an assembly body, the elections and appointments board. And I was appointed member. You can see my name under number 9.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. These are elections and appointments to what type of positions?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that period of time, personnel was quickly changing due to the war circumstances, and this also concerned appointments to positions of the heads of companies, administration institutions, and all those within the purview of the municipal assembly. As at that time state -- social property was proclaimed state property and in this particular case the municipality was in charge of appointing directors to the range of companies across the municipality. Most directors who were appointed were members of the majority party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. If you can keep that document. I'll come back to it in just a moment, but I want to cover one or two points I missed. Sir, you talked about the murder of a reserve policeman after the takeover. Did you witness that crime?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you speak to a person who was a witness to the crime?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see the investigative files regarding that crime?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be correct to say you don't know the circumstances of that murder or who the perpetrator was?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that would be correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you had also spoken in your direct examination about property being temporarily confiscated, property that was abandoned and used. Did you see Muslims and Croats leaving Prijedor on convoys over Vlasic Mountain? I'm not asking if you went on a convoy, but did you see those people gathering to get onto convoys in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: On one or two occasions, as I was passing outside the building that is today the Kozara museum, which is just across the way from the municipality building and the MUP, I did see buses taking busloads of civilians away. I saw people who were there to see those people who were leaving off. I don't know, however, which company exactly or which drivers were in charge of the transport or who the people boarding these buses were. My assumption was that they were headed for border crossings or on their way to territory controlled by whichever side they were thinking about crossing over to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, those people you saw, it appeared they were leaving with what they could carry. They had a bag. They had a suitcase. And that was the belongings that they were leaving Prijedor with. Correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Those were civilians, predominantly women and also a few men, and as far as I could see they had suitcases or bags. They would carry what they could physically carry with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it true that in order to leave Prijedor, individuals, particularly those who were held in the Trnopolje camp, had to renounce all of their property to Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of any such enactment that would have been issued and implemented. I only know that for a person to be able to leave Prijedor, would have to have a confirmation that they had paid all of their bills, utility bills. Then they would take that to the MUP and receive a permit or -- for travel, some sort of a document they would receive. I'm not familiar with the whole procedure. I don't know what they received from the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, I'm going to move back to the document, and I promise I'm getting towards the end. If you can look at the final point on S259. And that would be Roman numeral XVIII. Would it be correct that at this session of the municipal assembly of the 27th of August, 1992, presided over by Dr. Stakic, that there was a discussion on the security and political situation in Prijedor and that among those who participated in that discussion were Colonel Vladimir Arsic, Simo Drljaca, and Dr. Milomir Stakic?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is obvious that information on the political and security situation on the territory of the municipality of Prijedor was considered and that after the introductory remarks, there was Colonel Vladimir Arsic and the chief of the public security service, Simo Drljaca, who were guests. Also here I can see the names of those who took part in the debate. I remember that I participated in that particular session of the assembly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, at this particular session or at any other session presided over by Dr. Stakic that you were present at, did you discuss or did anyone discuss the murder of detainees in the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. At these sessions, we talked about political and security situation, about the possible reasons for this situation to get more complicated on the territory of the municipality. Some statistical information was presented by the centre for security services, and they were relevant to the perpetrators of traffic -- violations of traffic and the relationships with the population. It was never the -- on the agenda of the municipality to discuss the collection centres and further actions in that respect, nor did the assembly ever issue any conclusions with that regard. This was simply never the subject matter of any discussions or debates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you discuss at this session or any other the shelling and arson of homes in Hambarine on the 23rd of May, 1992 in Kozarac area on the 24th and 25th of May, 1992, and the casualties to civilians that occurred during these operations by the army?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, this was not the subject matter of the parliamentary debate, nor were any data ever submitted on such incidents. We were never presented any figures or any other kind of report of any sort.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever discuss the destruction of Catholic churches and mosques throughout the opstina of Prijedor but in particular, right in the city, in the town of Prijedor the destructions of the main mosque, the main Catholic church?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that the buildings that you have mentioned were destroyed during the war. I was working at the Impro, and as I was leaving for work, in the morning I saw the police who did not allow the general public to enter the street where the Catholic church had been and they explained that the road was not passable. I took a different road towards the railway station, and then along the railway line I went to the Impro building, so I did know that this had been done, that the church had been destroyed. However, who the perpetrators were, who the organisers of that crime were, I don't know. I was never in the position to see any documents to show me any data on who the perpetrators or organisers of those things were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, my question is only whether or not these incidents or these crimes were discussed in the municipal assembly during the sessions you attended. And if I'm correct, I understand your answer to be no. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never. We didn't discuss that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, in late July of 1992, the army conducted what is listed in the front page of one of the Kozarski Vjesnik articles as a Ciscenje in Brdo -- that the army planned a Ciscenje in Brdo. Did you discuss that in the municipal assembly, either in this particular meeting or any other meeting?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't discuss that at any assembly sessions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever discuss in the municipal assembly the massacre in late July of detainees in room 3 in Keraterm or the incident that was very well known in Prijedor of shooting, a long night of shooting at the Keraterm facility?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't discuss that in the municipal assembly. And as far as I can remember, the public media carried a story on an attempted attack by the detainees on the guards, and that's -- that was the reason why the shooting took place. However, this was never discussed in the municipal assembly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever discuss in the municipal assembly - I believe the session we're talking about is the 27th of August - the crime that occurred at Koricanske Stijene in a convoy leaving the Trnopolje camp in Tukovi and escorted by police in Prijedor where hundreds of mean -- approximately 200 men were lined up on a cliff and shot?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The municipal assembly didn't discuss that, and I don't have any knowledge or information about that event.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us of anything that Dr. Stakic did when he was president of the municipal assembly to prevent these crimes, to punish the perpetrators, to let people know what was happening so that some changes could be made?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the authority of the municipal assembly, he was not in the position to order either repressive or protection measures. As to whether he had any private contacts with anybody, I don't know. But in any case, this was not under his authority. It was under the authority of the police anything that has to do with the protection and security of citizens. It is the chief of the security centre who is responsible at the local level. And at the level of the republic, it is the Minister of the Interior who is responsible for that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I understand from your answer, you're not aware of anything that Dr. Stakic did to prevent, to punish, or to deter any of these crimes?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no information about any such activity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions. Thank you, sir. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I just want to take the occasion when you have in front of you this document. It's S259, XVIII. And can you please tell me why was it that Colonel Arsic and Mr. Drljaca took part in this discussion in the municipal assembly, being not members of this institution?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If my memory serves me right, the aforementioned persons were guests of the assembly. They didn't address the assembly on that occasion. And what their real role was when they appeared in the municipal assembly as guests, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Was this the only time that Mr. Arsic and Mr. Drljaca participated in sessions of the municipal assembly?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that this was the only time when the two of them attended an assembly session. If my memory serves me right, there was another representative of the military who attended as a guest on one or two occasions, but the assembly never discussed the military issues. It was only when we discussed the political and the security situation, then we would have guests. But those guests never gave any proposals to the assembly or discussed any matters before the assembly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You tell us this was a special event. Can you recall where these persons, especially Mr. Arsic and Mr. Drljaca, were seated in the room?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that the session was in the Rudnik hall and our guests were sitting in the front row on the left-hand side, the side that is reserved for guests rather than for the deputies themselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Was it the custom that guests could, as it is reflected here in this document at the right, to take part in the debate as all the others and it would appear in the document as a participation in the debate as all the other members of the municipal assembly?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that they had -- that they did say a few words about the political and security situation on the territory of Prijedor municipality. But I can't quantify the length of their contribution or the positions that they put forth on that occasion. In any case, they participated when discussing the matters regarding the military. And in any case, they would say about the things that compounded the political and security situation on the territory of the municipality, but that was all. They didn't make any other contributions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You would regard this document as you have it before you - one example, S259 - as a reliable document, or did you ever have doubts that on these minutes something was reflected what never took place?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: At every subsequent session of the assembly, the first item on the agenda was considering the minutes of the previous session and their adoption. There were occasions when deputies objected to the wording of the minutes, and most often it was just the wording, the technical mistakes in the minutes. I can't say that this is an authentic document that was presented to the deputies at this session of the assembly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So in other words, would you have reasons to believe that when we can read here that, for example, Colonel Vladimir Arsic took the floor twice, Mr. Drljaca took the floor twice, this would be correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say with any degree of reliability that that indeed was the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Once again, did you have reasonable doubts that documents as such were signed by Dr. Stakic and the accuracy of the copy certified by Dusan Baltic, that these were incorrect statements or incorrect certifications?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the book of rules governing the work of the assembly, any decision passed by the assembly is signed by the president of the municipal assembly, and this is certified by the signature of the secretary-general of the assembly and the stamp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: One thing is theory. One thing is practice. Was there any -- to the best of your recollection, was there ever a serious discrepancy between this theory, what you just -- that you just told us, and the practice?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a deputy, I was not in the position to know anything about that part. A deputy merely participates in the debate, votes in favour or against a certain conclusion or decision or similar things. The rest of the procedure lies with the municipal assembly and the committee for the publication in the Official Gazette.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Only for my better understanding: Following such a suggestion, you received the minutes of a session as a document?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. On -- during a subsequent session, we received minutes of the preceding session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: That was my question. And had you ever reason to believe that the content of this document you received on the next session on the previous session was incorrect?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember any deliberate mistakes or any blatant mistakes or any different interpretation of the discussions at the previous session of the assembly. There were some minor technical mistakes that were then corrected after the objections put forth by the deputies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. We need no longer document S259. Witness Vila, did you drive a car in 1992?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do have a car. I've driven since 1978, so I did pass the driving test. I have a driving licence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: My question was not whether you have now a car and whether you had a driving licence. My question was: Did you have and drive a car in 1992?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. At that time the situation was difficult. I did have a car, but I didn't drive it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Why didn't you drive your car?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reason was simple: The price of petrol was 6 German marks, and what a worker could make, as his salary was 2 German marks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I need to understand. Did you have a car for professional purposes or in your factory in 1992 did you have there any car?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had a vehicle, a Zastava 101. That was my personal vehicle. And I had a company car, a two-seater, and usually I drove myself to Novi Grad. I would go there to fetch the designs, and then I would bring them over to the production floor. So sometimes I would drive myself; sometimes it would be the professional driver who would drive that company car.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Was there any shortage of petrol at that time in 1992?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was a shortage of fuel. One couldn't obtain fuel freely at petrol stations. The retail prices were between 5 and 6 German marks, and the standard of living of the population at that time was very low and the use of cars was practically impossible. Most of the cars on the streets belonged to the military or to the police, and people who drove them were either members of the military or the police or members of the organs which were important for the functioning of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Would you need a certificate or permit to get petrol at that time, in 1992; to be more concrete, after the takeover?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you refer to me personally or my company?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: For your company or for -- whatever purpose -- when a citizen or any other person needed petrol, was it necessary to have a certification or permit to receive this petrol?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In most cases, like I've already told you, there were very few private vehicles on the roads. And one could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Could you please answer my question. I asked already twice whether when buying petrol at a petrol station you would need a permit or certification.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Have you ever been in Cirkin Polje?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am familiar with that neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Have you ever visited the Crisis Staff building in Cirkin Polje?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of the fact that the Crisis Staff was in Cirkin Polje. I was never in the Crisis Staff in Cirkin Polje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Have you ever seen a certificate or permit issued by the Crisis Staff in order to obtain petrol?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this was regulated. You knew how to obtain a certificate. But I have never seen any of these certificates, not a single one, and I don't know what it said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So would you regard yourself as a privileged person, opposed to others needing such a certificate?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said yesterday that from the 20th of May, 1992 onwards my company was not operating, so there were no privileges for me in the sense of using a car or being able to obtain petrol. I was definitely not in a privileged position because I didn't drive. I didn't use my car; therefore, I wasn't using petrol, between April 1992 and March 1993. It was only after I started working for the meat industry company called Impro that I had to use a car for business purposes, but sometimes even for business official purposes I was using public transportation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. The trial stays adjourned until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: One very small question based on document D54. We need not present it to you. If you recall, was Mr. Mile Mutic a member of the assembly?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that he was a member of the Democratic Party of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Democratic Socialist League.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did you ever meet Mr. Mutic besides the honour meetings of the assembly?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Do you regard this person as a reliable person?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know him quite well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: My question was: Do you regard him as a reliable person?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Is it correct that he was -- yeah, the other way around. In which way was he connected with Kozarski Vjesnik?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a while, he was the director of Kozarski Vjesnik. During the war, he was in a military unit, and today he is again the director of Kozarski Vjesnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: When did Kozarski Vjesnik appear for the first time?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think in 1973 or 1974. It has been a weekly paper since 1973 or 1974.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Mr. Mile Mutic, did he appear frequently in the sessions of the -- or attend frequently the sessions of the municipal assembly?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the period when he was not on the front line, he was present as a deputy. I don't remember exactly how many sessions he attended and how many sessions he failed to attend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Let's now turn to a separate issue. We have not yet admitted into evidence the document tendered yesterday by the Prosecution. This was the document provisionally marked S394B. May I ask first, as I indicated yesterday, the Defence whether or not the Defence received this document beforehand.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We received the document before, Your Honour, from the Prosecution, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The best possible original would be available?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. It's been provided to the Registry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May it please be shown, if it has not yet happened, to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We haven't examined the document, Your Honour, thank you. Would you like our comments if any?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We have a couple of things. First we would like to know the source or the origin in which the document was procured. There's nothing on the back side as we've seen from other documents. Secondly, we'd like if possible to get verification if the forensic handwriting expert was also provided off the top of our -- or my head, I can't recall if he was provided with this signature which purports to bear the signature of a Stakic Milomir. If he utilised that in the analysis. And if possible, the rationale why it was not provided to the forensic handwriting expert at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Let's discuss this later, because it's not related to the concrete witness statement. So I understand you object against the admission into evidence of this decision?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: For the given -- reasons given on previous -- similar occasions, this document is admitted into evidence as 394B-1, the original; the copy is 394B, as indicated yesterday; and the English version is S394A. May this document please be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Just to clarify. The general rules -- I don't know who made them -- are that the original stay with the evidence unit. We can provide a colour copy to the Court of the original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then it may be substituted by a colour copy and the parties be provided also, please, one colour copy to the Bench. Thank you. Once again, the question to you, Witness Vila: You are identifying your own signature?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I then ask that the witness be shown where is my stamp collection? Here it is - Exhibit S79B. For a moment I don't want to go into detail of the content of this document, but could you please have a look on the block of signature and stamp on the right-hand side, on the bottom of the page, and could you please explain for us what we can see there.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: What we can see is the signature and name of Dr. Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: If you will please compare. I think you have still available document S394, the best possible original. If it could be handed to the witness. Witness Vila, to the best of my recollection - and if the parties so want, I will find the page of the transcript - it was in yesterday's testimony that in the case of the absence of Dr. Stakic, a document would be signed by Mr. Savanovic?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, according to their respective competencies. The vice-president of the municipal assembly stands in the for the president of the municipal assembly in all the competencies of the president of the municipal assembly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: If you now could be so kind and compare the signatures on document S394B, the one page where you also -- we can find your own signature. Signatures 1 and 3, would this be such an example of signing the document while the president of the municipal assembly was absent? Would this be correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the absence of the president of the municipal assembly, the vice-president stands in for the president. Blank pages inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Pages 11385 to 11396.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So comparing the signatures 1 and 3 on this single piece of paper and the other document you have before you, 79B, would this document be signed by Dr. Stakic or by Mr. Savanovic?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not an expert in graphology. I'm not a handwriting expert, but as a layperson I think I can say that this is not the same signature as the one under number 1, Dr. Stakic's signature under number 1. It looks very much like signature number 3, though, but I can't say for sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You are no expert; absolutely correct, your statement. We can't demand to go into details when even experts cannot -- cannot come to a 100 per cent clear expertise. So may we now turn to -- for a moment to 79 only. You may read this document, please. We did already, but that you are aware of the content of the document. Did you ever see or hear about this concrete order previously?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: When the municipal assembly turned back to their regular meetings, isn't it your testimony that the municipal assembly ratified at that time all the decisions, orders, conclusions taken by the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did ratify. I can't tell for sure whether this order was on the same list. But in case it had been on the same list, then this decision too would have been ratified, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May the witness please be shown document S181. Just already page -- the first page of the Official Gazette, number 3 of 1992, dated Monday, 31 August 1992. Do you see item 120?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see it. I can't find it right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Could we please have the English translation on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I may be of assistance, Your Honour. [Interpretation] Mr. Vila, it's the number on the first page in the upper left corner.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is that 3/92?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just below that line you see number 120.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. I can see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Okay. Is it correct that later it reads: "All acts (decisions, orders, rulings and conclusions) adopted by the Crisis Staff of the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor or the War Presidency between 29 May and 24 July 1992 are hereby ratified"?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not sure that the original of the text given to the deputies has the same thing written, "order," or "decision." It is not quite clear from this decision whether the decision order was among the enactments that the deputies decided to ratify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I'm aware of this, and I will later confront you with this other document. But now is it correct that in fact on the Official Gazette of the Prijedor Municipality it reads: "All acts adopted between 29 May and 24 July 1992 are hereby ratified"?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Wouldn't it be correct that then also a order of 17th -- 17 June 1992 would be included in this decision?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it is on the relevant list. If included in the relevant list. In that case, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I don't discuss in the moment the relevant list. I discuss that what is reflected in the Official Gazette. Here it reads: "All acts, decisions, orders, rulings, and conclusions are hereby ratified."

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So it would be correct that also, as it's -- as we can read it here from the Official Gazette, this order would be ratified -- would have been ratified, the -- at its session of the -- of 27 August 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Was it for the municipal assembly or the Crisis Staff or the War Presidency to order to form a joint intervention platoon and ordering the Prijedor Public Security Station and the Prijedor regional command to do so?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This simply would have been unnecessary for the simple reason that within the purview of police work, the police is also supposed to protect the material, technical equipment, the population, and everything else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The question was whether or not it was in the framework of the -- of the mandate of the municipal assembly, the Crisis Staff, or the War Presidency to give orders as reflected here in this document to the Prijedor regional command to form a joint intervention platoon.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This would be outside the authority.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So it would be your testimony that this order in fact would be -- not be covered by the legal mandate given to these bodies; correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I take it from your testimony that you are not aware of this order. If you would have been confronted the 27th of August, 1992 with this order, would you have objected?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would have objected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. May then -- the other documents may remain with the witness. May we turn -- may we have in addition document S250 once more, please. Can we please proceed this way, as we did it yesterday, that always English version be put at the same time on the ELMO. May I ask you now as a at that time member of the municipal assembly, do you see discrepancies between the one document and the one published in the Official Gazette?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not been able to find the relevant order in this text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: If I may guide you to the second paragraph. Isn't it correct that it reads there: "In the period between 29 May and 24 July 1992, the Crisis Staff and the War Presidency passed enactments --" and then in parentheses "(decision/orders, decisions odluke rjesenja, and conclusions) which are hereby submitted to the Assembly for confirmation as follows"? Isn't it correct that it reads that this document may have - it's a question to you - may have formed the basis for your decision adopting all previous acts between 29 May and 24 July 1992, this same period of time covered by the decision published in the Official Gazette and this document, where it reads "Subject, confirmation of decisions within the competence of the municipal assembly adopted by the Crisis Staff"? Could you please try to find in this document S250 the decision we just discussed. That was the decision of -- on the intervention platoon, Exhibit S79 of 17 June 1992. Can you find it?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says in my copy "16 June" and then "23rd June."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So correct me if I'm wrong. Would it be the correct conclusion that this order from 17 June 1992 was not included?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to this list, it hasn't been included.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I may be of some assistance, because it's a bit hidden in our B/C/S version. [Interpretation] Page 8 at the very bottom of that page. You can't even see it very well. XXX Roman and then under number "1."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So this means that in fact you were at that time seized also with this order of 17 June 1992.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was not the whole order, just its title. The body of that order, its contents, were not available to the deputies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this clarification. Leaving all the documents with you, may the witness be shown Exhibit S77. Without any view to the contents of this document, let's first have a look on the signature and stamp block. Can you see any difference opposed to the previous document S79?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a stamp and a signature. But whether this is indeed Stakic's signature, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: But you would agree it's not the same signature as we found it on 79; correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't look like the same signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Looking now on the stamp, we -- what can we read there?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. The Municipal Assembly of Prijedor. Prijedor" in both the Latinic and the Cyrillic scripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And in the middle - it's better reflected on document 79, which no doubt is not signed [Realtime transcript read in error "is signed"] by Dr. Stakic - there we can see in the middle some insignia. What is the meaning of this -- these insignia depicted there?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my copy, I can't see it very well. The only thing that I can decipher is number 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Could, therefore, the witness please be shown the original of S79, which is available and photocopied.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. If I may just have a point of clarification. On the transcript on page 43, line 13, did the Court say "with respect to document 79, which no doubt is signed by Dr. Stakic"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Is not signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's what I thought. But the transcript reflects "is signed..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. As we are aware yesterday, we have absolutely been careful with the transcript at the moment. I don't know --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: One last point. On document 77, the English translation, there's clearly a typo on it because it references the date of June 1993, among other mistakes in the translation that's provided. Not on the top left-hand corner but in the body of the first paragraph. Just so the record is noted on that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We are aware of this problem. And as you may have seen yesterday, we try to do our very best to assist also the parties having reflected that what has been said on the transcript. So now, can you now see the middle of the stamp? What is depicted there, in the insignia you can see there?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the coat of arms of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and you can see a mountain, in front of it two chimneys. And on the side there are some ornaments. So this is the coat of arms of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And I would be interested to know why this mountain. Which mountain is depicted? Is this a special one, maybe in memorium of a special event or...?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I believe that the coat of arms represents the mountains of Bosnia-Herzegovina and its rich forests. And the chimneys symbolise factories, the processing factories. And the chimneys also represent development.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. You yourself mentioned that you could only identify the number 4 on this stamp. Isn't it true that on both documents, 79 and 77, we can read this number 4?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is clear, and I can read number 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Correct me if I'm wrong. Wasn't it there only one copy of a stamp with number 4 for the purpose of not abusing stamps, as it seems to be custom in most countries?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is customary for stamps to be marked by various numbers, to bear various numbers in various organisational units and that one number will correspond only to one organisational unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. May we then now turn to the content of this document. It reads that it's on quote "recommending to the Crisis Staff the manner of payment to and catering for the army and the police in the Prijedor municipality area." Can you say it is covered by the mandate of Crisis Staff, War Presidency, or municipal assembly?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know for a fact that this was under the authority of the Crisis Staff and of the War Presidency. But as far as I understand it, the army paid its regular units -- that is, it provided for its clothing, for its footwear, and for food. Now, whether the local community raised voluntary funds for the provisions, I don't know. I can't confirm that for a fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
