utterances.text: Was it for these bodies to charge Simo Drljaca with making a comprehensive review, as we can read it from this conclusion?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is what it does read in the conclusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Was it covered by the mandate of these bodies to do so, charging Simo Drljaca with making a comprehensive review?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that this is out of the scope of the mandate of this body.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May we then turn to -- back to document S250. And could you please have a look whether or not this conclusion can be found in this document from August 1992.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm having some difficulties locating the relevant part of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: 16 June. In case Defence counsel have identified this document already on -- if you may be of assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. We are searching the documents to find the various numbers of these stamps, so we are not -- we are not following the document. Give us one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Could you read Roman XII, "Enactments passed on 16 June 1992."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That is on page 8, Mr. Vila.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Here it reads: "Conclusion no. 02-111-198/92, assigning members of the Crisis Staff the duty of preparing a system of supplying food to the army and police troops." And then wouldn't it be correct to -- that this is in fact the document S77, the same number, same date?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So in conclusion, wouldn't it be correct to state that the municipal assembly adopted these conclusions, orders - I don't want to go to any further - documents mentioned in this document?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Is it correct that you yourself participated in the ratification of these previous decisions, orders?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I must say that these were just the title of these orders, decisions, conclusions without their contents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: All right. Would it be correct that also Dr. Stakic was seized with this decision reflected in document S250?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a deputy in the same way and to the same extent as all the other 90 deputies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Dr. Stakic was presiding over this session?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I believe that he was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So can you tell us why it was that just this document, S250, was not printed in total in the Official Gazette but that it read only "all acts adopted by the Crisis Staff are hereby ratified," without referring to the concrete acts, orders, rulings, conclusions?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know why this was done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May a reason be that at least some of these documents were previously printed in the Official Gazette no. 2 of 1992, these decisions, conclusions by the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Okay. Let's turn to another topic. Yesterday transcript page LiveNote 46, line 17 for following you stated: "The statute of the municipality contains an article governing the case of war or imminent danger of war when the assembly isn't able to meet as usual and as necessary. The article says that the Presidency of the assembly can be set up. I am not sure why they changed the name from Presidency of the assembly to Crisis Staff." So it would be a correct conclusion that in times of war and urgency or imminent danger of war, not the entire assembly would act but only the Presidency of the assembly; correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And you are not aware also of maybe reflecting this during the night why it was that instead of using the term "Presidency of the assembly" the term "Crisis Staff" was used?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally, I believe that it would have been better if the statute had been complied with and if the name had remained "the Presidency of the assembly."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So "Presidency of the assembly," this would be in concreto the following persons. Could you please give us the name of the present Presidency.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Members of the Presidency by the virtue of their positions are the president of the assembly, the vice-president of the assembly, and a number of others appointed by the municipal assembly from various departments or secretariats.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May the witness please be shown document S180, item number 19. May I first ask you: Did you participate in the meeting of 22 May 1992?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said yesterday that I am not sure that I attended this session but I said that I was at the sessions at which decisions, orders, and other conclusions were ratified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Independent from the question whether or not you were present at that meeting, if you have a look on the persons appointed as members of the Crisis Staff. Following your testimony. Dr. Stakic and Mr. Savanovic would be borne members as you stated the Presidency of the assembly now equaled with the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: How is it possible that we find on this list also the commander of the Municipal Territorial Defence staff, the Chief of Prijedor Public Security Station, the Secretary of Prijedor Municipal Secretariat for People's Defence? Was this covered by the statute, making reference to -- that in cases of emergency, the Presidency of the assembly would act instead of the entire municipal assembly?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that Mr. Stakic and Mr. Savanovic were appointed as the president and the vice-president of the assembly. They are supposed to be members of the Presidency or in this case of the Crisis Staff. The president of the executive board is a member of the executive part of government and should not take part in the legislative part of the assembly, and the same goes for the Territorial Defence and for the security centre. If one was to look strictly at the statute and the role of the Presidency, the Presidency should be made up of the president, the vice-president, and some of the deputies or presidents of the standing committees of the assembly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. The same document, if you would please have a look on the top page, item 18, "Decision on the organisation and work of Prijedor Municipal Crisis Staff." To the best of your recollection, did you attend this meeting, the 20th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I'm not sure whether I attended this particular meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: If you have a look on Article 6. Would it be under the mandate of the Presidency of the assembly to coordinate the work and activities of all components of All People's Defence, consider issues of mobilisation, development, and reinforcement of the armed forces and other organisations and foster their cooperation with other responsible municipal organs, and so on?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not a legal obligation or it is not within the purview according to the statute of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And if you have a look on Article 9 of the same document. "The Crisis Staff shall at all times cooperate with the army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Civil Defence, and Public Security through the senior officers or organs of these institutions."

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Article 9 -- that's exactly what Article 9 says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Would this be covered by the mandate of the Presidency of the assembly?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This would have been outside the scope of the Presidency's authority.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then only a final question related to this document: On the top of this document of the Official Gazette of Prijedor Municipality, it reads "year 1." Was there no Official Gazette of the Prijedor Municipality in the year 1991?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose that there was. Every year you had the Official Gazette.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Would it be a wrong assessment that -- stating "year 1," that it's to demonstrate that a new period began for Prijedor in 1992, or what was the underlying reason to add it "Official Gazette of Prijedor Municipality, year 1" in 1992?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The obligation to publish the Official Gazette is prescribed by the law. Now, why this reads "year 1," I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Was this a decision taken in any of the bodies you were a member of?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the decision to put "year 1" here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember any such decision being made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Another topic: Yesterday LiveNote page 67, line 18 you stated: "I remember President Cehajic's statement on the radio that he would put up Gandhi-like resistance, meaning that he would not take part in this whole thing." To the best of your recollection, when was this that you heard President Cehajic on the radio?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was on the same day or the day after the takeover.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This would be April 30 or 1st of May; correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I know that this question was already put to you, but let me try again. It was the president of your municipal assembly - you were a member of this assembly - weren't you interested in the fate of Mr. Cehajic?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The assembly did not discuss this, nor did we have any information concerning Mr. Cehajic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: But wouldn't it be natural that you would be interested as a member of this body what is the fate and what's the reason why Professor Cehajic never appeared again?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was wondering at the SDA and HDZ deputies why they didn't come to the new founding sessions to raise that issue themselves, because they too were legitimately elected and appointed deputies during that particular term of office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: What would you understand by the notion of "Gandhi-like resistance"?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In as far as I'm familiar with the term, it implies struggle by silence in order to achieve a certain aim or a certain interest. This probably refers to a long-term struggle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So it would be a non-armed resistance; correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I should suppose so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Finally once again, as you sit here, you don't know about the fate of President Professor Cehajic?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know his fate. But after people who had previously left moved back to Prijedor, I never heard that he came back, but I know that his wife did. I don't know any of the other details concerning his fate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The 29th of April did you participate in any meeting or demonstration or conference of special nature?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did you get a new ID the 30th of April, 1992 allowing you to enter the building of the municipal assembly opposed to Professor Cehajic?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did have a new deputy's ID, but I'm not sure if this was done for the first session or for one of the subsequent sessions of the assembly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Do you still have this ID?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not on me right now, and I'm not sure if I've kept it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: But it's your testimony that immediately after the takeover, a new ID was issued for you; correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Was it a special ID for members of the municipal assembly?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It had the same shape and the same size for all deputies containing personal information and a photograph of the deputy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Isn't it true that at the same period in time, immediately after or on the date of the takeover, IDs were also issued to other bodies or other organs or other institutions such as the police, the bank, the executive board?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't know for sure whether other institutions and organisations changed their IDs too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Who gave you this new ID?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The technical services, the secretary of the municipal assembly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Have you been at Cirkin Polje the 29th, the 30th of April?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You're aware that there maybe was a meeting at Cirkin Polje?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Are you aware that IDs were issued at Cirkin Polje at that period of time?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe that any IDs would have been issued at Cirkin Polje, because they just didn't have the technology, the equipment it took to produce IDs. You usually have specialised services and units that issue documents and produce these documents and the IDs, and I'm not sure who was in charge of what you were talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Have you ever seen one of your colleagues from the SDA or HDZ with such a new ID?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they did not take part in the prolonged part of municipal assembly sessions after the takeover, and I have no idea why they didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: In yesterday's testimony, LiveNote page 48, there was a broad discussion on the notion of the "artificial creation," or better, "Muslims as an artificial creation." Do you recall that you testified yesterday on this issue?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: On page 49, line 4 you made reference to different censuses, 1961, 1971, 1991. Was it possible for a citizen in Prijedor to declare himself or herself in handwriting as a Muslim, Serb, or Croat, or wasn't it true that on -- let's call it on the ballot or on the document that had to be filled in it was already printed the -- the categories had already been printed whether a person would identify him or herself as a Muslim, as a Serb, or as a Croat?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly all the information that the ballot contained, but there is one box which says "nationality" or "ethnic group," which means that the subject of the census must identify himself as belonging to one of the ethnic groups. Whether all the different ethnic groups were offered so that anyone could circle what they identified themselves as or whether there was a blank space left for the person to add their own ethnic background, I can't really remember, since there have been no censuses since 1990.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You said "1990." I think 1991 would be correct; correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1991. Correction, 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Coming back to this quotation of Muslims being an artificial creation. To the best of your recollection, in what newspaper, as far as you know, did you read this quote?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was in the local papers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And this would be Kozarski Vjesnik?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kozarski Vjesnik, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And it is your testimony that you can now after ten years recall having seen this special expression? I'll put it this way: "Muslims as artificial creation."

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember the text exactly, the exact wording. I can't even remember if Dr. Stakic actually said this or if maybe the journalist who wrote the article added this himself. I really don't know, so I can't confirm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Judge Vassylenko, you have additional questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Yes, I have some. Mr. Vila, you testified that after the takeover in Prijedor, a person had to have ID and work assignment in order to travel through the Prijedor municipality. What is it, a work assignment -- what is the correlation between work assignment and duty obligations which were introduced in Prijedor municipality after the takeover?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The law prescribes that the Ministry of the Army through the Department for Military Issues across the towns in case there is a mobilisation, that they should mobilise manpower and materiel and technical equipment in the percentage and to the extent specified in an order from the ministry, from the republic. The remaining military-aged men receive work assignments by a special decision in their company or institution -- in the same company or institution in which they had worked up to that point in order to secure continuation of services for all these companies and institutions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: And is it the same, work assignment or duty obligations?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: It's the same. And then what authority introduces this work assignment or duty obligations in Prijedor municipality?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The companies or their administrative body or organ, in coordination with the Ministry of Defence or one of its departments, they would coordinate and agree which of the military-aged men would receive a work assignment, the Ministry of Defence, one of its special departments. But if the army requires a higher degree, a higher grade of mobilisation at any given point in time, then part of those who had up to that point held work assignments become mobilised for the army. But that's only if there is -- if the degree of mobilisation increases as required by the army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Okay. But in Prijedor municipality, what body -- what, let us say, official body adopts a decision on introduction of work assignment or duty obligations?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: War assignment is a legal obligation. It's prescribed by the law. The Ministry of Defence is in charge of the relevant records and all the other issues, the Ministry of Defence and its department in Prijedor, its branch is Prijedor branch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: But again, you testified about war assignment or work assignment?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Work. Work assignment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Work. And it was my understanding also that you said about work assignment. And in Prijedor -- why the Ministry of Defence decided about work assignment?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Ministry of Defence in cooperation with the directors of the different companies and administrative bodies within these companies harmonised their respective data as to who was holding the work assignment. And then the Defence department or the Ministry of Defence would issue mobilisation papers, and the administrative body would issue a certificate concerning the work assignment or the engagement of a particular individual in a certain company or institution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: A decision on work assignment existed after or before the takeover in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In earlier periods, we had drawn up plans on what to do and how to function in case of war across the board in the companies and institutions, and what it said is that according to the degree of engagement, the companies and institutions should be manned by all the available people who were not mobilised into the army, into the military.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Your enterprise received a work assignment?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my testimony yesterday, I said that the company where I worked simply ceased to operate on the 20th of May 199 -- correction, went on collective vacation, collective leave on the 20th of May and thereafter never resumed work, because we were working with foreign partners and due to war, the foreign partners stopped their -- stopped all their commissions. It is within the competence of the executive board and the director of the company to decide who is in charge of providing for the minimum of activity by the company, and then this is verified or ratified by the relevant ministry department.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: I understand. But did you receive work assignment before 20th of May; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, I'm not sure about the exact date of when work assignments began, but my own work assignment was signed by the director general of our company and then this was ratified, this was accepted by the Prijedor Department of the Army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: But who ordered your director to introduce work assignment?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The hierarchy is determined by a plan according to which the company functions in wartime or under the imminent threat of war. Each company has a plan of functioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Okay. I -- next question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think it's appropriate to have a break now. The trial stays adjourned until ten minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Of course. Judge Vassylenko, I interrupted you before the break. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Mr. Vila, have you ever been to Omarska or other defence facilities in the Prijedor municipality?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never been even in the near vicinity of the centres that you have mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Have any of your friends and neighbours, subordinates, or acquaintances were mistreated, arrested, or detained in Omarska or other detention facilities between May 1992-September 1992 in Prijedor municipality?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: During those events, I couldn't know who was in those centres. It was only on the return of some people in 1996 I spoke to some of my acquaintances and they told me they had been there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: But in 1992, you were not aware about these facilities and the detention of people in these facilities?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the media there was information for the general public that a certain number of people were in the investigation centres or in the collection centres. I don't know what term exactly was used. And the intention was to find out whether they organised paramilitary units and whether they instigated some things on the ground that would lead up to war conflicts. I didn't have any more information on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: You told us that Dr. Stakic was elected to the Prijedor Municipal Assembly as representative of the Radical Party, founded by Veljko Guberina.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that yesterday, and I learnt that about a month or two months after the first session of the assembly at the beginning of the work of that assembly, I didn't have that information. I only learnt that subsequently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: But can you explain us how it has happened that Dr. Stakic being elected as representative of Radical Party was appointed as vice-president on behalf of SDS?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but I believe that that Radical Party, founded by Guberina formed some sort of a coalition with them. And Dr. Stakic is a native of Omarska, where Serbs are a majority, and he received support from these people. I am not sure what the real reasons were and how the two parties reached this agreement on the appointment of Dr. Stakic to that position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Did you know Dr. Milan Kovacevic?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew him from the municipal assembly at the time when he was given the mandate as the president of the executive board of the municipal assembly. After that, I would see him at the sessions of the municipal assembly in his capacity as the president of the executive board, he would introduce the motions tabled by the executive board for the adoption by the municipal assembly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: And if compared with Simo Drljaca, what was -- your assessment, what was the intellectual level of Dr. Kovacevic?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacevic was very professional in the execution of his tasks. Sometimes he would appear rough in the treatment of other people. However, if one talked to him for a bit longer, you would see that he was a moderate person. As for Simo Drljaca, one could say that he was a very short-tempered person, that he had a very short fuse, and he didn't listen too much to either his superiors or to his subordinates for that matter and that he had a propensity to act of his own will, not to listen to the advice of other people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: But what about their intellectual level? I mean, Simo Drljaca and Dr. Kovacevic, how you assessed their intellectual level. It is low, high, average, super high?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that he was a person of an average intelligence. Both of them had a university degree. In order to obtain a university degree, you have to have an average level of intelligence, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Before you stated that Dr. Stakic also has an average intelligence, and how can you explain that persons of average intelligence were elected to the Prijedor Municipality leadership, not other people with higher intelligence?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were difficult times. Most of the intelligentsia and intellectuals sort of escaped responsibility, fled from responsibility because they didn't want to take any risks, and they knew in advance that they would be taking risks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Well, I have no more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Judge Argibay, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Vila. I will try to go back to one thing that I want a clarification on it. Yesterday you told us - I'm not asking yet. I'm repeating -- quoting what you said yesterday - that there were soldiers coming back from the front that would carry weapons. Some lines under that statement you said that there were certain groups who were prone to looting. Today again you mentioned looting. And you told us that in your building you formed a group to guard -- to protect the building and its neighbours. And a little later - I think it was a question by the Defence counsel - you said that this was, or something like that, a common practice in Prijedor during -- that was the question. You said that you think there were a number of buildings where similar measures were being taken. Do you know what happened in other cities or villages or hamlets around the municipality of Prijedor? Was this also a practice by civilians, as you told us, to protect the buildings, the neighbours, something like that?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I know the situation, there were people in the villages who were afraid, regardless of their ethnic backgrounds. They were afraid of the possible attacks of paramilitary groups and possible slaughters and similar things. So in other villages and towns it was customary for the civilians to set up night guards that were in place to send certain signals if they noticed a group of unknown people coming.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: How would you make a difference -- I'm sorry, Judge -- the Presiding Judge also told me that I have not quoted the page on yesterday's transcript, and the problem is I have not a copy of it. But it was -- the question was the first one at 15.13.26, just for the Defence to -- and the Prosecutor to look at it. Sorry. I'm coming back. Then how would you make a difference between these groups self-designated to protect the other civilians as night guards and what you recently said in this same page, some lines up, a paramilitary group? How you would tell the difference between one and the other.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Night guards in the buildings were organised by the tenant councils. They would not leave the buildings. It was their task to stand guard during the night and record anybody who left the building or entered the building. And if those people didn't know the person who tried to enter the building, they had the right to ask for their ID. These groups of neighbours did not carry arms. They just had a copy of the key for the front door. And if somebody turned up at the door, they would ask their name and they would ask for their ID. There were incidents on the territory of the municipality when some rogue soldiers carrying arms would be involved in the murders of people. There were Serbian girls murdered by Serbians. There were murders who have in the meantime been elucidated. There are some which have never been elucidated. I've just mentioned that as an example of things that were happening at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: So the question -- the problem and how you make the difference between these groups of civilians and this, what you call, paramilitaries was that these were unknown people to you.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: What you called paramilitaries. They were unknown people. And this was, as you stated some lines before the last page, that was customary around the villages of Prijedor municipality; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The Defence, please. Further examination by Mr. Lukic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Once again, good afternoon, Mr. Vila.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you a few questions arising from the questions of my learned friends from the Prosecution and the Honourable Judges.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would like the usher to show the witness Exhibit No. S394, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here you can see a conclusion. And above the signature, you can see that this is a conclusion passed by the presidents of political parties and presidents of the groups of deputies. As far as the SDS is concerned, who was its president at that time?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. It may have been Miskovic, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the person under number 2.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who the president of the group of SDS deputies was?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time it was Mr. Savanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see the presidents of other parties and presidents of other party groups on this list?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Under number 6, Aiz Grabic. He represented the Socialist Alliance of Youth or the Party of Private Initiative. Under number 7, Dragan Svraka was from the same party, from the Party of Private Initiative. Under number 8, I can see my name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you the president of the party or the president of the group of the deputies?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was the president of the group. Under number 9, Milena Vokic represented the group of the deputies of the Reformist Party. Under number 10, Nebojsa Bogunovic represented the same party, the Reformist Party. Under number 11 and under number 12 are representatives of the HDZ. Number 4 and 5 are representatives of the SDA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Mr. Mujadzic the president of the party for Prijedor, of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether he was the president for Prijedor or for the region. One of those things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about Husein Crnkic? Was he the president of the SDA group?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a deputy. I don't know whether he was the president of the group or the representative of the group of the SDA deputies. I don't know for a fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we then agree that the positions of the SDS president and the president of the group of SDS deputies are here represented under number 2 and number 3 in the persons of Simo Miskovic and Dragan Savanovic?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Stakic Milomir, therefore, on this list does not belong to either of these categories as a representative of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was usual for the president of the assembly and the presidents of the political parties and the presidents of the groups or chair people of the groups should discuss issues and host meetings or chair meetings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I don't know whether it's due to misinterpretation or a wrong statement. On page 66, it reads: "The president of the assembly," and we are referring now to 22 January 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At that time Mr. Stakic was the vice-president of the municipal assembly. I would now like the usher to show the witness Exhibit S79, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document mentions the establishment of an intervention platoon. Are you aware of the fact that there was an intervention platoon commanded by the Crisis Staff and later on by the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I am not aware that something of that sort existed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it usual for every battalion to have an intervention platoon?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said yesterday that I am not very familiar with the army. But while doing my regular military service and in conversations with others who were in operative military units, I found out that there were certain groups which were sent in advance of certain military operations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Today we spoke of various signatures and stamps. Do you know whether the stamp or stamps were in the possession of the president of the municipal assembly or whether they were with the secretary of the municipal assembly?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was usual for the stamps to be with the secretary of the assembly because he was the one who used the stamps when dispatching documents and signing certain documents that had to do with payments.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Later on we will come back to this, or rather, we can proceed right away.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... the next documents. So S064, S066, S068, S069, S070, S072, S080, S081, S394.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Just for the registrar, S66 was admitted as J4.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us, Mr. Vila, that a certain number on a stamp referred to a particular service. On the stamp that we have seen, we could see the number "4." Can you see number "4" on this stamp or a different number?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there is a number that's clearly visible, and that's number "3."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you put it on the ELMO, please, the original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please, what is the number of this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's S64B.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: No. It should be. So, therefore, that we are not confused, S64 is another document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's not your mistake, Mr. Vila. Can you look at the document now, document S64, and tell us the number that is visible on the stamp, if you can see it.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not quite legible. I don't know whether it's a "3" or "5."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it's definitely not "4"; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. It's not "4."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could we now see the document no. S66 or J4.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you see a number on this stamp?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can see, the number is "8."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When we blow it up on the computer, we can see that it's "3." But it's definitely not "4"; is that so?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not "4."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can the witness be shown document no. S68, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is less legible. But if you could.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, again, it looks like either a "3" or an "8."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: S69, please.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, there's a number here which is either "3" or "8."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When we blow it up, we can see that it's "8," so you are right.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's "3."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: S80, please.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It looks like an "8" to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you now look at document S394 and compare the signatures. The signature on document 394, under number 1, and the signature on document S80.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the second document, underneath the word "president," it says "for," and then there is a signature, which means that somebody was signing for him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it's obviously a different signature.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's not identical under number 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the stamp is one we have seen before, number 8.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please now compare the signature under number 3 with -- from document S394 with this signature.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, these two don't look alike either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this signature does not belong to the vice-president of the municipal assembly, if we compare these two documents.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I'm able to tell, they don't look alike.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... and show the witness Exhibit No. S81, please. And to put the same document, S394, to compare.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please tell us the number on the stamp.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's visible here. It's "4." And the signatures, as far as I can tell, are different.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this signature differs both from number 1 --

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: And number 3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From document S394 and from number 3 on document S394; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And would the usher please be so kind and show the witness number S048, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you tell the stamp number on this stamp?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The number is not legible. I don't know whether it's "2," "3," or "8."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And whose name is written there, although there's no signature?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Travar Ranko, who is the Secretary for Agriculture.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We have now finished with this quick research into various stamps and signatures. On page 54, Their Honours asked you -- that is, His Honour Judge Schomburg asked you whether after the takeover of power you immediately received an identifying document, identity papers. And when you replied that you received your identity papers on the first or second session of the municipal assembly, what identifying document were you referring to?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was referring to my deputy's card.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is your identity card different from this card?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. The deputy's card has a number on one side and the photograph of the deputy, his name, and on the back it states the rights and the immunities of a deputy, and then it's put into a plastic cover. It's plasticised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you -- did you ever ask for a new identity card?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I think it was in 1993 or 1994. But I can check that because -- no, I've left it in my hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: An identity card is a document that all citizens have; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The deputy's card is a card that only deputies in the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor have; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. As a deputy in the municipal assembly, did you have to keep track of orders issued by the municipal assembly?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our duty was when summoned to a session to acquaint ourselves with the material, the amendments that we had received in writing, or to give proposals orally as to certain modifications or amendments to the material to be discussed. Apart from deputies elected to municipal commissions or committees deputies had no other duties, and the commissions dealt with certain areas, and there was a group of deputies of each party which would meet before a session to take up standpoints on certain issues, and then either as a group or electing one person to represent them they would do that, but you were able to have your own opinion as a deputy. This was not prohibited.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a member of a commission, did you also have to follow the orders of the municipal assembly?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The election and appointment commission, of which I was a member, worked according to orders by the municipal assembly. It was presided over by the president of the commission based on interparty agreements on the distribution of certain mandates. The personnel commission at a session of the local parliament would bring proposals to the assembly concerning certain appointments and nominations, but only within the purview of the local assembly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the same time when you were a deputy and a member of the election appointment commission, you were a director of an enterprise, a company, were you not?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These different duties did not collide, at least not according to the then-existing legislation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was not our question, but thank you for this explanation. However, as the director of a company, did you follow the instructions of the municipal assembly or of the director general, whoever your direct superior, according to the hierarchy inside the enterprise, the company?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The overall activity within a company is run according to the internal hierarchy of the company itself. Contacts with the municipality were most often limited to contacts with the Secretariat for the Economy. This contact was usually related to obtaining certain approvals, authorities, statistics regarding production raids, business results, that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Secretariat for the Economy is part of the executive bodies of government, and the head of this secretariat is a member of the executive board; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If someone was a member of the Crisis Staff and at the same time the director of a company, by virtue of being the director of a company or in his -- in the person's position as the director of the company, would that person then follow the instructions received from his direct superior directors or from the Crisis Staff? What's your opinion, even if you were not a member of the Crisis Staff yourself?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The director was gainfully employed in whatever company he was working for, and he would answer to the board of managers and to his superior director.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If someone was, for example, a member of the Crisis Staff and at the same time the chief of the Public Security Station, would that person then follow the orders of the Crisis Staff or the orders of his superiors in the chain of command in the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the then-existing laws, the head of the police -- the chief of police would answer to the -- to his superior minister, the Minister of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would like now the usher to show the witness document no. S77, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I use the meantime to ask the parties what's your assessment about the necessary remaining time for the Defence and the -- maybe the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 10, 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I think about the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So unfortunately it's impossible to conclude today. But please proceed for the next three minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your company on the 16th of June, 1992 was not operating. That's what you told us.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We worked until the 18th of June, which means for another two days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean May?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Excuse me. I meant the 18th of May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time did any other companies or institutions operate? For example, the bakeries, the Prijedor bakery?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Companies like Zitopromet for processing wheat and the bakery to a lesser extent were operating. The Impro meat industry company was also operating. The Prijedorcanka [phoen] company, the fruit company, some parts of the iron ore mine in Ljubija, all the hauliers, the Autotransport and the Autoservice, the transport companies also to a lesser extent, or the capacity of their activity was smaller than -- the paper factory was also operating.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for this comprehensive elaboration. We did not expect you to remember all the details. Was it necessary to provide bread for the army at that time? Because you said that the bakery was operating.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to my information, the military commands would close contracts, make contracts with certain factories or companies regarding the supply of certain items. Now, whether in Prijedor the army had any such contractual relations with any of the companies and what the exact extent of these contracts was, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When someone was mobilised -- when a person was mobilised and sent off to the front line, was it common practice for that person to keep receiving their salary in the company where they were employed -- gainfully employed?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the first period, some people were receiving two salaries, because they were receiving a symbolic salary as members of the army and also back in their own company. Later on all they were left with is the money, whatever money they were receiving from the army, or clothes and food. At some point it was only clothes and food and no longer money. However, their employment was frozen, and the only thing that was still being paid was the contributions to the pension funds. And even this was done only by those companies who could afford to do that. But many of the companies simply couldn't afford.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does all of this apply to reserve policemen? Please tell us if you know.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think more or less the same thing applies to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think our time has just run out and we'll finish for today. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Please understand that the same rules are valid today as I told you yesterday, not to contact parties, maybe witnesses, or the Defence counsel. We'll meet again tomorrow then in the afternoon at quarter past 2.00. The trial stays adjourned until tomorrow at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 30th day of January, 2003, at 2.15 p.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25
